newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Handelsbanken ambitious in Estonia market.
newsitem.headline: Handelsbanken ambitious in Estonia market.

text.p: Largest Swedish bank Handelsbanken on Monday said it aimed for a big market share as it became the first foreign bank to enter the Baltic corporate finance and brokerage market by buying an Estonian broker.
Handelsbanken said it had bought 100 percent of broker Aktoris although it did not name a price for the deal.
"Our intention is to be a significant player in the local market here," Bo Kragh, head of Handelsbanken's Tallinn office, told a news conference.
The Handelsbanken move comes as foreign interest in the financial markets of Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania is growing.

Although the markets are small compared to the West, investors have achieved high returns and they are expected to develop fast as they complete the transition from former Soviet republics to market economies.
Handelsbanken said it aimed to capture some 10 percent of the Estonian broking and corporate finance market.
The Swedish bank was also eyeing the neighbouring markets of Latvia and Lithuania.
"We have a long-term commitment to the Baltic countries," Kragh said.
Kragh also said the move by Handelsbanken would bring faster development to the Baltic financial markets.

"Although it is quite true that we will be competing with the local banks as regards corporate finance and the ...stock exchange, we also believe in a way we will be assisting the growth of the total market," he said.

"We hope that we can encourage foreign investors to this market and as a consequence the market should grow for everybody and attract additional interest to the market and therefore be a boost to the stock market here."
Aktoris managing director Auli Kumpulainen said the deal would allow Aktoris to sell the services of its large Swedish investor.
"The aim is to be able to provide more efficient products in in the Estonian investment sector," Kumpilainen said.
But she conceded that the Baltic markets were still small for foreign investors.
